narrative_purpose: Makes the chapter's evolutionary clue visible: Prolemuris carries partly fused upper limbs that appear to bridge Pandora's common six-limbed body plan and the Na'vi's four limbs.
subject: A three-subject naturalist comparison plate on one ground line. At left stands a generalized Pandoran arboreal animal with six fully separate limbs: two forelimbs, two middle limbs and two hind limbs, all visibly attached separately to the torso. At center stands a Prolemuris-like climbing creature with two hind limbs and two upper limb trunks; each upper trunk clearly forks below the elbow into two separate forearms and hands, creating four hands from two shared upper arms. At right stands a tall slender Na'vi silhouette with exactly two arms and two legs. All three face the same direction in neutral side three-quarter pose, with no overlap between bodies.
scene: A dark xenobiologist's field-plate ground with faint forest haze and a few low glowing fronds for scale, no dramatic action.
camera: Straight-on full-body comparison at matched shoulder height, each subject entirely visible from head to foot.
light: Soft cool bioluminescent rim from low flora, even enough that every limb attachment and fork remains readable.
palette: Global cool Pandora palette with teal-cyan anatomical rim light; neutral stone ground and no competing warm focal area.
style: Painterly speculative-zoology naturalist plate, anatomically legible and observed, not a movie still.
detail_level: High on shoulders, elbows, fork points, hands and limb attachments; faces subdued; background minimal.
composition: Three separated figures ordered left to right from six separate limbs, to forked paired upper limbs, to four total limbs, with open dark space above each for labels.
consistency_notes: Limb counts are load-bearing: left exactly six separately attached limbs; center exactly two legs plus two upper arms that each fork into two forearms and hands; right exactly two arms and two legs.
negative_prompt: no text, no arrows, no wrong limb counts, no extra arms, no fused silhouettes, no ape or monkey from Earth, no photographic or 3D-render look, no action pose
